summary: The ruling totalitarian political party of North Korea, exercising absolute control over state, military, and society under Kimilsungism-Kimjongilism. Its Central Committee departments formulate strategic national directives, foreign policy, and economic allocations.

The chief policy-making organ of the Workers' Party of Korea between sessions of the Central Committee. It gathers top party secretaries, regional leaders, and military commanders to ratify state policies and personnel rotations.

The supreme inner executive council of North Korea, comprising the top five officials in the country. It wields day-to-day decision-making power across the party, military, government, and state security apparatus.

name_en: Central Military Commission of the WPK
summary: The supreme military decision-making body of the Party, directing the Korean People's Army and national defense policies. It authorizes strategic missile tests, military force posture changes, and war preparation drills.

The most powerful executive bureaucracy in North Korea, controlling cadre appointments, political surveillance, and ideological vetting across party, government, and military cadres. Control of OGD secures decisive administrative dominance over the elite.

The party department managing state media, public indoctrination, cultural productions, external psychological operations, and the Kim family personality cult. De facto supervised by Kim Yo Jong, it coordinates official statements and regime messaging.

The central party apparatus governing the research, engineering, and manufacturing of ballistic missiles, conventional weapons, and nuclear warheads. It oversees defense production facilities and manages arms deliveries to foreign allies including Russia.

The clandestine financial network managing overseas businesses, foreign exchange earnings, and luxury acquisitions directly for the Kim family. It commands state trading monopolies, gold exports, mineral smuggling, overseas labor, and illicit revenue schemes.

The supreme policy leadership body of the state, enshrined in the constitution to direct national defense, state security, and foreign affairs. Chaired by Kim Jong Un as President of State Affairs, it is the primary state-level executive authority.

The unicameral parliament of the DPRK, formally passing legislation, approving state budgets, and ratifying cabinet appointments. Between sessions, its Standing Committee performs constitutional duties and receives foreign credentials.

The civilian executive government organ charged with implementing national economic directives, managing state factories, and supervising civil ministries. Premier Pak Thae Song was appointed in December 2024 to oversee state economic production.

The administrative defense ministry overseeing KPA logistics, defense infrastructure, international military cooperation, and arms procurement. Re-headed by No Kwang Chol in October 2024, it handles state-level military diplomacy.

The party's political commissariat embedded throughout the armed forces, enforcing ideological orthodoxy, party discipline, and absolute political obedience to Kim Jong Un. Its political officers countersign all military orders down to battalion level.

The operational combat command headquarters of the Korean People's Army, planning war operations and directing ground corps, naval flotillas, and air wings. Led by Chief of General Staff Ri Yong Gil, it executes military doctrine and border maneuvers.

The strategic branch of the Korean People's Army operating nuclear and conventional ballistic missile regiments. Formed in 2012 as an independent branch, it controls intermediate and intercontinental ballistic launch sites.

The specialized administrative and technical bureau revealed in early 2023 to direct North Korea's advanced ballistic missile programs. Under General Jang Chang Ha, it coordinates design, serial manufacturing, and field trials across missile divisions.

The principal secret police and counter-intelligence organ of the DPRK, answering directly to Kim Jong Un. It carries out domestic ideological surveillance, hunts defectors and foreign spies, monitors ruling elites, and runs the political prison camps (kwanliso).

The national civil law enforcement agency responsible for public order, crime investigation, residency registration, and internal travel travel permits. It operates local detention centers and the network of forced-labor re-education camps (kyohwaso).

North Korea's primary clandestine intelligence agency responsible for foreign espionage, covert sabotage, assassinations, and global cyber warfare. Formed in 2009 by merging party and military spy units, it reports directly to the SAC and Party leadership.

The offensive cyber warfare department of the Reconnaissance General Bureau, staffing specialized military cyber personnel. It conducts destructive intrusions against foreign government infrastructure, critical services, and defense targets.

State-sponsored cyber threat cluster executing major cyber-heists, cryptocurrency theft campaigns, and ransomware attacks under the Reconnaissance General Bureau. Sanctioned globally for stealing billions of dollars to fund North Korea's prohibited WMD programs.

The premier state arms dealer and proliferation vehicle of the DPRK, marketing ballistic missile technology, conventional weapons, and military hardware internationally. It serves as the primary conduit for military export contracts with Iran and Syria.

The ministry responsible for conducting foreign policy, international negotiations, and overseas mission operations. Under Minister Choe Son Hui, it steers bilateral ties with Russia and China while maintaining hostile rhetoric toward the United States and South Korea.

The central military research and development body, historically termed the Second Academy of Natural Sciences (SANS). It designs ballistic missiles, rocket propulsion engines, guidance electronics, and nuclear weapons delivery vehicles.
